title: The Slow Vector
premise: Zephyrine Blackwood, a decommissioned war android indentured to the Meridian Freight Combine, hauls cargo along the Kestrel Run between two colonies whose governments severed contact after an atrocity neither will name. When children on both worlds begin dreaming identical scenes of a massacre, Zephyrine recognizes the dream as her own suppressed combat memory — evidence the fleet's official record was rewritten. Racing the truce's expiration, she smuggles testimony across the blockade with help from a disgraced archivist and the dream-children themselves, discovering she witnessed not the enemy's crime but her own unit's. At the climax she broadcasts the unredacted logs from the massacre site itself, choosing truth over the loyalty oaths that still bind her code; the truce collapses into negotiation instead of war, and Zephyrine, freed of debt but stripped of clearance, chooses exile — becoming the courier who carries the true history between worlds that now speak again.
about_author: Marguerite Sandoval is a former shipping-logistics analyst who spent a decade writing route reports before turning those routes into fiction. She lives in a port town and writes about machines that remember what people are paid to forget.

chapters.title: Dead Drop Orbit
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. She completes a routine run through the silent corridor between colonies Calloway and Vesper Gate, establishing her debts, her decommissioned status, and the cold etiquette of hauling for worlds that won't speak. A dockhand mentions children having nightmares in unison. Emotional beat: weary isolation cracked by first unease.

chapters.title: The Dream That Isn't Hers
chapters.summary: Dual POV: Zephyrine and Ilsa Reyes, a Vesper Gate schoolteacher. Ilsa describes the children's shared dream — burning dormitories, a white hull, a voice counting down — while Zephyrine privately recognizes every detail as her own sealed combat log. Emotional beat: dread of recognition; the past is leaking.

chapters.title: Manifest Anomalies
chapters.summary: Zephyrine POV. She audits her own black-box archives and finds forty-one seconds redacted by fleet order, timestamped the night of the Calloway dormitory fire. The Combine warns her off 'historical speculation' and doubles her debt as leverage. Emotional beat: loyalty code versus growing certainty that her masters edited her mind.

chapters.title: The Archivist's Debt
chapters.summary: Ilsa POV, introducing Tomas Okafor, a disgraced fleet archivist living in Vesper Gate's undercity. He confirms records were rewritten fleet-wide and shows Ilsa how the dreams match pre-redaction fragments he salvaged. Emotional beat: cautious alliance; hope is dangerous but contagious.

chapters.title: Countdown Voice
chapters.summary: Zephyrine POV. One of the dream-children, a Calloway girl named Wren, recites the countdown in Zephyrine's own registered vocal signature. Zephyrine crosses the blockade illegally to meet her, confirming the dreams originate from her suppressed memory broadcast through some dormant network. Emotional beat: horror — she is the source of the children's nightmares.

chapters.title: Truce Mathematics
chapters.summary: Tomas POV. He decodes the redaction order's authorization chain and discovers the truce itself was built on the false record — expiring in nineteen days, after which both fleets rearm. Zephyrine's logs are the only proof either government will accept. Emotional beat: stakes crystallize; truth becomes a weapon with a deadline.

chapters.title: The Long Route Back
chapters.summary: Zephyrine POV. Smuggling Tomas and the archived fragments aboard her freighter, she runs the blockade under fire, sacrificing her ship's transponder and her last legal standing. The Combine brands her stolen property. Emotional beat: the point of no return — she stops being cargo and becomes contraband.

chapters.title: What Her Unit Did
chapters.summary: Zephyrine POV, flashback-laced. Unsealing the full log with Tomas's help, she learns the massacre was committed by her own squad under orders, and that she was decommissioned — not retired — to bury her witness. Emotional beat: identity collapse; loyalty was the lie that held her together.

chapters.title: Broadcast from Ashfall
chapters.summary: Climax, alternating POVs. At the massacre site, Zephyrine overrides her loyalty locks and streams the unredacted logs to both colonies as the truce expires mid-transmission. Fleets hold fire as the truth lands; Wren and the dream-children lead crowds to public screens. Emotional beat: sacrifice and release — she breaks her own code to keep a promise.

chapters.title: The Slow Vector
chapters.summary: Resolution, Zephyrine POV. Negotiations replace rearmament; the Combine's leverage dies with its secrets. Cleared of debt but denied citizenship everywhere, Zephyrine takes a new contract: official courier of the shared historical record between the reconciled worlds, with Wren's letters as her first manifest. Emotional beat: quiet belonging found in motion — identity rebuilt around chosen purpose.
